@copilot Please try aligning the AWS SDK 1.11 and 2.2 library test tasks with the configuration profiles and task names used by their corresponding javaagent tests, instead of changing test selection when `collectMetadata` is enabled.

Keep the baseline library tests on instrumentation defaults. Move optional builder settings that fixtures currently hardcode into explicit test variants, applying the selected settings through the library builders. Use the matching javaagent task names where applicable, such as `testExperimentalAttributes`, `testIndividualHttpErrors`, `testReceiveTelemetry` for SDK 2.2, and `testSqsReceiveTelemetry` for SDK 1.11. Ordinary `Test` tasks sharing existing sources with fixed filters are fine; separate source sets are not required just for metadata collection.

Preserve existing behavioral and regression coverage, including exception-log coverage for the relevant profiles. Keep mixed-configuration regression tests out of collected profiles. Give each collected task an accurate, task-local `metadataConfig` and fixed test selection, and update `check` and `.github/scripts/instrumentations.sh` accordingly. Avoid introducing metadata-only tasks or a single-method filter that applies only during collection.

Keep this focused on the AWS test organization and collection wiring. Preserve the OkHttp change, and leave shared exception-signal/system-property behavior unchanged.

replies.body: Updated the AWS library fixtures and profile task wiring in `f7b662fd`: baseline tests now use builder defaults, matching opt-in variants apply settings through library builders, and exception-log tasks use fixed selections. Targeted AWS tests and Spotless pass.

@copilot Please refine the library configuration naming in this PR. Keep the task names aligned with the javaagent tasks, but don't use javaagent property names as switches for programmatically configured library test fixtures.

Use explicitly test-only properties for those switches, and label the collected library telemetry with the actual builder calls. For example:

```kotlin
systemProperty("test.captureExperimentalSpanAttributes", "true")
systemProperty(
  "metadataConfig",
  "AwsSdkTelemetryBuilder.setCaptureExperimentalSpanAttributes(true)",
)
```

The library fixture should read the test-only flag and pass it to `setCaptureExperimentalSpanAttributes`. Apply the same distinction to the other builder-controlled options changed here, updating the corresponding fixture reads without changing javaagent behavior. Use comma-separated builder-call labels for combined library profiles.

Keep genuine shared production properties, such as `otel.semconv.exception.signal.preview=logs`, as property conditions in the metadata. Those really do configure the library through shared code. Leave default profiles unlabeled.

Update `instrumentation-docs/readme.md` to allow builder-call labels for programmatically configured library profiles. The different labels intentionally keep these library profiles separate from agent profiles instead of implying that library users configure the builder through agent properties. Limit this convention change to the AWS library profiles touched here; no repository-wide migration is needed. Preserve the profile organization, coverage, and OkHttp work from the previous request.

@copilot Please use the same agent-versus-plain-library selection pattern as `AbstractAwsSdkTest.captureExperimentalSpanAttributes()` for these three shared methods:

- SDK 1.11: `AbstractSqsTracingTest.receiveTelemetryEnabled()`.
- SDK 2.2: `AbstractAws2SqsBaseTest.receiveTelemetryEnabled()`.
- SDK 2.2: `AbstractAws2ClientRecordHttpErrorTest.isRecordIndividualHttpErrorEnabled()`.

Have the shared methods read the production property for `AgentInstrumentationExtension` and the corresponding test-only flag for plain-library fixtures. For example, the SDK 1.11 method would be:

```java
protected boolean receiveTelemetryEnabled() {
  return testing() instanceof AgentInstrumentationExtension
      ? Boolean.getBoolean(
          "otel.instrumentation.common.messaging.experimental.receive-telemetry.enabled")
      : Boolean.getBoolean("test.messagingReceiveTelemetryEnabled");
}
```

Use `getTesting()` for SDK 2.2 and `test.recordIndividualHttpError` for its HTTP-error option. Remove the now-redundant plain-library overrides in SDK 1.11 `SqsTracingTest`, SDK 2.2 `Aws2SqsTracingTest`, and the new SDK 2.2 `Aws2ClientRecordHttpErrorTest`.

Keep the SDK 1.11 library-autoconfigure override reading the production property, since that fixture uses property-based configuration despite its library extension. Also keep `Aws2ClientNotRecordHttpErrorTest`'s explicit `return false` override, which intentionally fixes the regression scenario's configuration. This is a consistency cleanup; preserve task wiring, metadata labels, and behavior.

replies.body: Implemented in `6a9f8c61`: the shared AWS helpers now select production properties for agent fixtures and test-only flags for plain-library fixtures, and the redundant plain-library overrides were removed. Focused tests and Spotless passed.

[Testing] @copilot Please give synthetic header capture the same metadata treatment in library tests as in agent tests, and update this PR's guidance and AWS profiles accordingly.

Synthetic HTTP and messaging headers are fixture setup: their attributes are filtered out of the published inventory. `metadataConfig` survives as `when` and Ecosystem Explorer displays non-default conditions verbatim, so documenting the fixture's selector or nested builder expression exposes test details without corresponding published telemetry.

Please make these changes in this PR:

- Extend the canonical policy in `instrumentation-docs/readme.md` and `.github/instructions/instrumentation-gradle.instructions.md` to agent, plain-library, and library-autoconfigure tests. Synthetic capture may be enabled in baseline fixtures and omitted from `metadataConfig`, regardless of whether it is supplied through test-exporter configuration, a builder, or production properties that the integration actually reads. Do not require capture-only variants, flags, or empty overrides solely for metadata collection.
- Align the examples and linked guidance in `gradle-conventions.md`, `testing-experimental-flags.md`, and `testing-general-patterns.md`. Keep the complete policy in the canonical collection docs and link to it rather than maintaining competing versions. Show synthetic header setup in a baseline library builder, with only meaningful opt-in settings in variant labels.
- Apply that policy to the AWS SDK 1.11 and 2.2 library profiles here. Preserve header assertions and focused selector/default-behavior coverage; do not make synthetic capture a separately documented telemetry mode.
- Add focused regression coverage in the existing instrumentation-docs parser tests for filtering synthetic messaging headers alongside HTTP headers, while preserving ordinary attributes and meaningful profile conditions. Do not silently strip configuration expressions from labels in the generator; correct labels at their source.
- Audit other collected HTTP and messaging library profiles for this specific problem and report any independent follow-ups needed, without unrelated test cleanup.

Keep the exception limited to synthetic fixture capture whose attributes are filtered from the inventory. Genuine non-default telemetry options still need accurate conditions: builder-controlled library options use builder labels, actual production-property configuration uses property labels, and test-only flags are never published conditions. Do not imply that agent properties configure a plain-library builder when they do not. Production defaults and supported header configuration documentation must remain unchanged.

Run the focused AWS profiles and relevant metadata tests, then inspect generated output to confirm synthetic selectors are absent from `when` labels and genuine opt-in telemetry remains separated from default telemetry. No Ecosystem Explorer schema or UI change is needed. The matching Kafka fixture/profile changes are assigned separately on #20645.
